pairs.locus: Hugo of St. Victor, Soliloquium de arrha animae (ANIMA / HOMO)
pairs.question: Multum, fateor, collatum est mihi, sed quaeso te, si ut (asseris) ego jam assumpta sum, quid adhuc differor, quoniam ad amplexus sponsi necdum venire possum?
pairs.answer: Nescis ergo, anima mea, nescis quam foeda prius fuisti, quam polluta, quam deformis et squalida, discissa et dissipata, omni horrore et enormitate plena.
pairs.derivation: ANIMA's whole speech is one plea ending in a genuine interrogative (quid adhuc differor...?); quoted verbatim and contiguous. HOMO's reply is dropped of its vocative-free framing only by normalizing; answer = the reply's first full sentence, which directly answers why she is delayed (she was first foul and must be restored). Cut before 'Et quomodo tam cito...' where HOMO elaborates.

pairs.locus: Hugo of St. Victor, Soliloquium de arrha animae (ANIMA / HOMO)
pairs.question: Nunquid ille est dilectus meus? Quaeso, dic mihi, ut sciam an ille est, ut si denuo ad me venerit, obsecrem eum ne recedat, sed semper permaneat.
pairs.answer: Vere ille est dilectus tuus qui visitat te, sed venit invisibilis, venit occultus, venit incomprehensibilis.
pairs.derivation: ANIMA closes her speech with a direct question; quoted as the self-contained final interrogative (with its 'Quaeso, dic mihi' plea, whose 'ille' = the sweet unseen visitor she has just described). HOMO answers directly with his first sentence affirming it is indeed her beloved; cut before 'Venit ut tangat te...' where he elaborates on the manner of the visit.
